messages:
Alex (AE): Heads up — ACME POC hitting 413s when they call /v1/generate. Repro steps from their side: single POST with ~3.7MB JSON payload (lots of docs in prompt). They see: 

Customer-Eng (ACME): "curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 413 Request Entity Too Large
Response body: {\"error\":\"request entity too large\"}"

Maya (SE): Do we know where the 413 is coming from? nginx/proxy cutoff or our app? Can they share raw content-length header?

Customer-Eng (ACME): Sending the request example now. Content-Length: 3887643. They also POST via their internal gateway (nginx) -> our edge LB -> api.redwood.ai. Not using gzip.

Jamal (Infra): Likely upstream/nginx or LB rejecting. Our API gateway has default max body allowed; dedicated trials sometimes hit proxy limits if their proxy sits in front. Also note some CDNs strip chunked encoding.

Sasha (SalesEng): For context, they're tightly coupling ~120 docs into a single prompt to get one-shot extraction. They were hoping to avoid embeddings pre-indexing.

Maya (SE): Quick checks: 
- Is the client setting Content-Encoding? gzip would help. We accept gzip if header is set. 
- Recommend chunking the prompt or using embeddings + retrieval to avoid giant single request.

Alex (AE): Can infra temporarily bump their proxy limit for this dev test? The POC needs to run end-of-day.

Jamal (Infra): I can request a temp increase for the dedicated trial instance. Need the instance id and approx max size. Also note increasing limit is not a long-term fix; we should recommend architecture changes.

Customer-Eng (ACME): Instance id: ded-9a2f. If we bump to 10MB they'll be unblocked. What's the security impact?

Jamal (Infra): 10MB is fine for short window. I'll put request in. infra-bot: submitted change request #INC-4321 to our edge team to increase max_body_size to 10M for ded-9a2f for 4 hours.

infra-bot: change request INC-4321 created by Jamal (Infra) — awaiting approval from edge team.

Maya (SE): While infra handles that, here are two concrete, short-term dev fixes for ACME to try: 
1) Gzip payloads: reduce size dramatically. Example: 
```
# client-side
printf '%s' "$PAYLOAD" | gzip > request.gz
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Encoding: gzip" --data-binary @request.gz
```
2) Chunk the context: split docs into N smaller prompts and either (a) call model iteratively accumulating state, or (b) index via /v1/embeddings + semantic retrieval then send only the top-k passages in prompt.

Sasha (SalesEng): On the pricing side the customer asked whether switching to embeddings adds cost. Short answer: embeddings + retrieval adds embedding calls and storage but dramatically reduces generation token cost. For POC we can estimate: ~120 docs => one-time embedding cost, then <1 generation call per query. I'll draft a quick cost comparison.

Customer-Eng (ACME): Good, can you share a minimal chunking example? They want to avoid re-embedding during POC.

Maya (SE): Minimal chunking pattern: send each doc as a separate small prompt and keep a light conversation context with summary tokens. Example pseudo: 
```
# pseudo-workflow
for doc in docs:
  response = POST /v1/generate prompt=\"process doc: {doc}\"      # small
  store summary
# final request
final = POST /v1/generate prompt=\"consolidate summaries + question\"
```
This keeps per-request payloads < 200KB in practice.

Jamal (Infra): Edge team approved INC-4321. Increased max_body_size for ded-9a2f to 10M for 6 hours. They'll notify when change is live.

infra-bot: INC-4321 approved and applied to ded-9a2f — change live.

Alex (AE): ACME ran test with gzip and small chunking and now the request goes through. Thanks team.

Customer-Eng (ACME): Confirmed — unblocked. Also following up: what's the model context limit we should assume? They were worried about max_tokens param truncating input.

Maya (SE): max_tokens controls output length only. Input (prompt) size is limited by model context window; depends on chosen model (8k, 32k, etc.). For POC pick a 32k model if they need big context, but better long-term: embeddings + retrieval.

Sasha (SalesEng): Action items: 
- I’ll send a short email with the cost comparison (embeddings vs one-shot heavy prompts).
- Maya to share gzip & chunking examples snippets.
- Jamal to confirm infra rollback time (6 hours) and note for the customer.

Alex (AE): Thanks all. Will update ACME and close the POC blocker. :thumbsup:
